newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees swings in Asia sugar import needs.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees swings in Asia sugar import needs.

text.p: German statistician F.O.Licht sees a prospect of wide swings in future world sugar import demand as a result of plans to raise output in Asia.
Licht said in a report that trade flows are constantly shifting with new surplus and deficit regions emerging.
In Asia, rapid growth of output in Thailand had made its sugar, both white and raw, "an important feature in the world market..."
Indian output had meanwhile risen to levels where surplus but high cost production had put producers in a no-win situation.
If they chose to export they were at risk of losing money but if they chose to stock they would still lose out financially.
Licht says output in China is set to fluctuate, though it appears to be on an upward course once more, and the country seemed likely to remain a net importer for the time being.
As well as the three giant Asian producers - India, China and Thailand - Licht cites what it calls another important group of countries, all producing in excess of a million tonnes a year.
The three - Indonesia, Pakistan and the Philippines - were all major consumers with collective annual needs in excess of eight million tonnes.
Licht said that in these circumstances "it is clear production swings can have an important effect on the world market".
All three countries made announcements from time to time about new plans to increase production.
The results might be somewhat unpredictable, but if they met with success this time round it "could result in a substantial drop in total world market import needs".
